references.text: The sons of Machir, the son of Manasseh, went to Gilead and captured it, driving out the Amorites who lived there. Moses gave Gilead to Machir, the son of Manasseh, and he settled there.
Machir, the firstborn of Manasseh and father of Gilead, was given land because he was a warrior; he received Gilead and Bashan.
Half of Gilead, along with Ashtaroth and Edrei, the cities of Og's kingdom in Bashan, were given to the sons of Machir, half of Machir's descendants.
Machir, the son of Manasseh, is mentioned in connection with Joseph's family, and his descendants received Gilead as their inheritance.
The clan of Machir is listed among the descendants of Manasseh, and Machir was the father of Gilead.
